agent.result_text:
The rollover change is in and its test passes. One of the four tests in the spec still fails, on a bug that was already there and has nothing to do with the rollover.

**The change** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/PeriodService.java`)
- After the rollover writes its `ROLLOVER` line, it now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open (not closed or soft-closed), in start-date order.
- Each period goes through the same steps as a soft close by hand: the same figures are fixed, the same event fires, and the same `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED … period=<name> total=<n>` line is written. To share that code, I moved the body of `softClose` into a private `softCloseFixing` method. A soft close by hand works exactly as before.
- No front-end change was needed.

**`bin/e2e` result: 3 passed, 1 failed**
- The main "rollover soft closes" test passes, including the exact audit lines (2026-11 was already closed, so it is skipped, and 2026-12 shows `total=1.00`). Scenarios 1 and 2 pass too.
- **Scenario 3 fails at `acceptance.spec.ts:2052`.** It never runs a rollover. It looks at crew C1's pool shares as of 2026-03-28 and expects Ada at `33.34`, because C1 had three people that day (Ada, Cam, Ben). The app shows `50.00`. I didn't re-run it with my change taken out, but the cause is in code my change doesn't touch:
  - When Cam is merged into Ben on 03-30, `CrewService.merge` deletes Cam's crew-membership row, so nothing records that Cam was in C1 earlier.
  - `PoolService.crewPools` also drops anyone who isn't on the sheet today, even when showing a past day.

Fixing it means keeping a record of crew memberships that a merge ends: a new stored column, changes to the merge and to the past-day pool view. That is a separate feature, so I've left it alone.

Decision for you: should I fix the crew-history bug as well so the whole spec passes? It would add a database column and change how merges and the past-day pool view work.
